extracted.intended_audience: RWHAP (Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program) recipients and subrecipients; HRSA/OMB reviewers; public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and operational guidance for the HRSA Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program HIV Quality Measures (HIVQM) Module information collection, including who must/should use it, what data elements and measures are included, reporting frequency, burden estimates, and how to comment on the ICR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of clinical quality management programs (statutory requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: RWHAP Parts A, B, C, and D recipients and subrecipients must follow statutory requirements for the establishment of clinical quality management programs to assess the extent to which their HIV services are consistent with the most recent HHS Clinical Treatment guidelines and to develop strategies to improve access to quality HIV services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are expected to operate clinical quality management programs that measure consistency with HHS Clinical Treatment guidelines and develop improvement strategies; the HIVQM Module was created to assist recipients in meeting this clinical quality management program requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the HIV Quality Measures (HIVQM) Module (voluntary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HIVQM Module is an online tool HRSA created to assist recipients in meeting clinical quality management requirements by allowing recipients to input data for the HRSA performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the HIVQM Module is voluntary for RWHAP recipients. The module is accessible via the RWHAP Services Report, an existing online portal that RWHAP recipients use for required data collection of their services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measures coverage and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: HRSA maintains over 40 performance measures across the following categories: (1) core, (2) all ages, (3) adolescent/adult, (4) pediatric HIV, (5) HIV-exposed children, (6) medical case management, (7) oral health, (8) AIDS Drug Assistance Program, and (9) systems-level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients can choose the performance measures they want to monitor and enter data accordingly; the module supports a broad range of clinical and programmatic measures across multiple populations and service areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relating financial data to performance (2 CFR 200.301 requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HIVQM Module supports the requirement imposed by the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for HHS Awards that recipients relate financial data to performance accomplishments for their federal awards (2 CFR 200.301).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should use the module to connect program financial information to performance outcomes as required under HHS uniform administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data entry frequency and reporting cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may enter performance measure data into the HIVQM Module four times a year and then generate reports to assess their performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly data entry enables recipients to generate recurring reports for performance assessment and quality improvement monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for population-specific data and subset measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have the option to enter data for specific populations for a subset of performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows disaggregation of measures by population groups and focused monitoring of particular subpopulations when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking and comparison across jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may compare their performance to other recipients in their state, region, and in the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarking functionality is provided to help recipients set goals, monitor performance relative to peers, and identify improvement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for participation in Medicare/Medicaid incentive programs
rubrics_metrics.description: For recipients and sub-recipients participating in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid incentive programs (e.g., Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program and the Merit-based Incentive Payment System), the HIVQM Module may be used to monitor the HRSA measures that qualify and comply with the requirements to receive incentives from these programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients engaged in these incentive programs can leverage HIVQM to track measures that map to incentive program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change to demographic field: 'Sex at Birth' replaces 'Gender'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Gender" will be removed and replaced with "Sex at Birth." The available response options are: "Male," "Female," "Unknown."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a proposed modification to the collection and was the specific change explained in response to requests for clarification during prior notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden definition and estimated respondent burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden includes the time to review instructions; develop, acquire, install, and use technology and systems for collecting, validating, and verifying information; train personnel; search data sources; complete and review the collection; and transmit the information. The total annual burden hours for this ICR are summarized in the provided table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on pilot testing of the HIVQM Module, the average burden per response declined from 1 hour to 0.2333 hours (approximately 14 minutes). Table: HIVQM Report — 2,063 respondents, 4 responses per respondent, 8,252 total responses, 0.2333 average burden per response, 1,925 total burden hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of likely respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Likely respondents are RWHAP Part A, Part B, Part C, and Part D recipients and their sub-recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the entities expected to supply data to the HIVQM Module and to be subject to the related clinical quality management requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment procedures and deadlines for the ICR
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on this ICR should be received no later than December 19, 2025. HRSA submitted the ICR to OMB for review and approval and comments submitted during the first public review will be provided to OMB; OMB will accept further comments during its review and may act only after the 30-day comment period for this notice has closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written comments and recommendations should be sent within 30 days of publication to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain by selecting 'Currently under Review—Open for Public Comments' or using the search function; to request a copy of clearance requests, email paperwork@hrsa.gov or call the HRSA Information Collection Clearance Officer.
